title: RentGuard Renters Policy — Limit on Rental Residences per Customer
content:
## Guideline

A customer may hold RentGuard Renters Policy coverage on at most 2 rental residences at once — for example a family apartment and a student unit — with one policy per rental address, counted across every renters policy in the customer's name.

Only live policies count toward the limit: a renters policy that is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal. A policy that is cancelled or expired does not count.

## Condition for binding a new policy

Before a new RentGuard policy is bound, the customer holds fewer live renters policies than the limit of 2 and none at the same rental address.

- **Evidence.** The condition is judged from the company's policy records — the renters policies held under the customer's profile, their status and their rental address — as they stand before the new policy is bound, not from the customer's description of what they hold.
- **Object.** The count runs over the customer, the person to whom the new policy is to be issued.

## Checklist of the condition

| Live renters policies already held by the customer | A live renters policy already at the new rental address | Condition met |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | no | yes |
| 1 | no | yes |
| 1 | yes | no |
| 2 | — | no |

## Hypothetical cases

- A customer holds one in-force RentGuard policy on an apartment and one cancelled policy on a former address. Only the in-force policy is live, so the customer holds 1, fewer than 2, and a policy on a new, different rental address meets the condition.
- A customer holds one policy in force and one pending nonrenewal on two different addresses. Both are live; the customer holds 2 and a third policy does not meet the condition.
